title: A sequence in Sequential Function Chart: fill, then mix
summary: Complete a Sequential Function Chart with three steps by adding the missing timed transition, and check that the valve and the mixer never run together.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence with one 10 ms task; they do not establish process volumes, mixing quality, valve timing on real equipment, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Read a Sequential Function Chart as steps that are active one at a time, actions that run while their step is active, and transitions that move the activity.
Add a timed transition that uses the elapsed time of a step.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/FillMix.sfc.json the steps IDLE, FILL and MIX, their actions and the transitions IDLE to FILL (Start) and MIX to IDLE (after a delay) are drawn. Add the missing transition from FILL to MIX with the condition step_fill.T >= T#50ms, where T is how long the step has been active.
stages.checkpoint: The sequence runs IDLE, FILL, MIX and back to IDLE on each Start, with one step active at a time.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Start is pressed at {{t:10}} ms. The step changes on the scan after the condition becomes true. Predict Valve and Mixer at {{t:20}}, {{t:80}} and {{t:140}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:FillMix.Valve=true,FillMix.Mixer=false@20|Valve ON}} at {{t:20}} ms; {{v:FillMix.Valve=false,FillMix.Mixer=true@80|Mixer ON}} at {{t:80}} ms; {{v:FillMix.Valve=false,FillMix.Mixer=false@140|both OFF}} at {{t:140}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starter has the three steps and two of the three transitions: FILL never leaves, so the valve stays open and MIX never runs; add a transition from FILL to MIX whose condition is step_fill.T >= T#50ms.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named FillMix and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:70}}, {{t:80}} and {{t:130}} ms: the valve closes and the mixer starts in the same scan at {{t:80}} ms, and the mixer runs for {{t:50}} ms before the sequence returns to IDLE.
stages.checkpoint: The valve and the mixer are never ON together. A second Start at {{t:160}} ms repeats the cycle.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Which step is active while the valve is open, and why can only one be active at a time? Change the MIX action to open the valve too and see which assertion fails.
stages.checkpoint: Each action sets both outputs, so a step defines the whole output state and the sequence cannot leave an output on by accident. The scenario shows the sequence logic only; it does not show process feedback such as a level switch.

hints.text: A transition has a source step, a target step and a condition. The transition from IDLE to FILL is already there; copy its shape for FILL to MIX.
Add a transition with fromStep step_fill, toStep step_mix and the condition step_fill.T >= T#50ms.

faultCases: The starter has the three steps and two of the three transitions: FILL never leaves, so the valve stays open and MIX never runs; add a transition from FILL to MIX whose condition is step_fill.T >= T#50ms.
